projects.title: [CUSA] Crimson Raiders Discord Bot
projects.meta: Discord Bot developed in Python for CUSA
projects.desc: This background check bot system was one of many I did for this bot, mostly to automate a bunch of HICOM duties. It works essentially by going into an empty Roblox alt account via that account's token, and searching up the user inputted. It checks things like Account Age, Friend count, Badge count, Group count, and then goes through all of the user's friends - parsing their names to find any names similar to the original account name to see if they can be flagged as alt accounts. For example, if robloxuser was friends with robloxuser_alt, the bot would detect that and flag it as a suspicious alternative account. The bot will allow for a count of one maximum red flag before failing the user's background check - and logging it in a private channel for HICOM to see.

projects.title: coldd Development Marketplace Bot
projects.meta: Discord Bot developed in Python for coldd
projects.note: Based off of HiddenDevs' marketplace bot
projects.desc: This was a very extensive system I did for a company I co-ran, "coldd Development". It spanned about 3k+ lines of code in Visual Studio Code prior to its optimization, created in mid-2024. It was essentially a remake of HiddenDev's (.gg/hd) old marketplace posting system bot. It entailed some simple devex commands (/devex-robux, /devex-currency), etc. The main premise of the bot was the very extensive marketplace system, which had three options: "Hiring", "For-Hire", and "Tutorial". Tutorial walked the user through how to use the system, although, I will admit it was improved later. Hiring and For-Hire began the post preview system, [Fig.1] which helped the user customise their post before sending it to mods for approval. The customization system included things like a description, title, a contact method, a payment type, a role (Scripter, Builder, etc) and images. After the user was satisfied with their creation, they'd submit it for review with an ID - and moderators would either deny or approve it with a custom embed [Fig.2]. All in all, for slightly earlier in my discord bot coding existence, it was the hardest bot I've ever made and pushed me far out of my comfort zone (my skills are vastly different compared to 2024).
